Instrument (EN): Digital Well-Being — Miao's researcher-developed two-domain teacher scale
Scales / measured domains (EN): Individual digital skills and behaviour (6); Subjective digital perception and stress (6, reverse-coded). Two-factor research model; not interchangeable with DWBS-Wang2026-12.
Research provenance: Miao J. Front Psychol 17:1999813, published 2026-10-26, DOI 10.3389/fpsyg.2026.1999813. Online convenience/snowball single cross-sectional Chinese university physical education teacher sample N807. Original research-team-designed instrument based on Gui et al 2017; alpha total .864, dimension alpha .81/.81; item-level CFA CFI .995/TLI .993/RMSEA .019, AVE .42/.41 below .50; no independent replication or strong convergent validity.
DB locales: No matching published respondent version in live app.assessment_versions: 149 unique published keys, 234 versions (EN154/RU80/ES0), checked 2026-10-27. Distinct from existing Master Wang DWBS-12 Chinese undergraduate cohort row3911.
EN form: English article is NOT proof of an independently validated English respondent version; final administered language and official EN respondent wording not established.
RU form: No validated RU-RU respondent translation in this study.
ES form: No validated ES-ES respondent translation in this study.
Other translations: China study setting does not establish a separately validated ZH-CN linguistic adaptation or final respondent language; original research form only.
Target population: University physical-education teachers in six Chinese provinces/municipalities N807; occupational university setting, nonrepresentative, not clinical diagnosis.
Commercial digital use / permission revi: Frontiers article CC BY, but full instrument reproduction/commercial digital administration, scoring and potential third-party underlying items are not individually cleared. Obtain author's written confirmation, approved exact 12 items, keyed reversals and commercial electronic permissions before use.
Validated edition evidence / links: https://doi.org/10.3389/fpsyg.2026.1999813 ; comparison separate DWBS-12 https://doi.org/10.1177/13591053261490980 ; COSMIN https://www.cosmin.nl/
Verification notes / safety gate: PRELIMINARY original instrument, not independent cross-cultural validation. Cross-sectional association not temporal/causal; moderate convergent validity. Names/12-item count shared with separate Wang DWBS-12 but not semantically identical; keep separate keys. No copyrighted item wording/algorithms/cutoffs or Supabase/site activation.

Instrument (EN): Individual Problems and Strengths Scale (STIC) — independent Norway eight-factor psychometric audit
Scales / measured domains (EN): Flexibility/resilience (3); Life functioning (2); Open expression (2); Self-acceptance (2); Disinhibition (3); Negative affect (6); Self-misunderstanding (2); Substance abuse (2). Original 8-factor structure; scales NOT equally reliable.
Research provenance: Original IPS section of Pinsof et al Systemic Therapy Inventory of Change (STIC), 2009, NOT an original 2026 questionnaire. Zahl-Olsen R et al, J Clin Psychol 82(9):1378-1387, online 2026-06-05, DOI 10.1002/jclp.70164; first independent CFA N841 Norwegian couple/family-therapy clients data 2010–2016; eight-factor better than alternatives, variable reliability; substance abuse alpha .20. Supporting public dataset/article 2021 DOI 10.1016/j.dib.2021.107577 includes 22 items in N841 same sample (do NOT double count).
DB locales: No corresponding live published IPS-STIC assessment in app.assessment_versions (149 keys/234 versions EN154/RU80/ES0). No existing exact source/key in 4070-key Master or PR495 386-reference index.
EN form: Existing original STIC English language not a NEW independently tested EN respondent form; electronic form, respondent wording, proprietary STIC rights unverified.
RU form: No validated RU-RU respondent translation established.
ES form: No validated ES-ES respondent translation established.
Other translations: Norwegian clinical study shows psychometric use in Norway but does not, alone, document an independently validated Norwegian translation; NO validation claim withheld.
Target population: Norway psychotherapy clients N841, ages 12–72, across couple/family therapy settings incl minors; same N841 as 2021 dataset, not independent replication sample.
Commercial digital use / permission revi: Original STIC/IPS instrument copyright/licensing and approved digitization/reproduction/scoring NOT cleared by an open-access research article or public dataset. Clinician-governed tool only after legal, measurement and risk review including suicide/self-harm, harm to others, substance use, and consent for minors.
Verification notes / safety gate: EVIDENCE record for pre-existing IPS/STIC instrument, not novel questionnaire. Eight factors structurally favored but multiple 2-item/low-alpha subscales, substance abuse alpha .20. Includes suicidality, violence, substance use; clinical escalation required. No independent language validation, public self-test, published questions/score keys, Supabase/site changes.
